title: Picture book
rule: A children's picture book: large flat shapes, one simple sentence per panel.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p86_picture_book.py (cut paper: kit/cutpaper99.py; agent and clock: kit/build_page02.py; stranger: build/p64_window_in_window.woman)
made: eight HANDMADE cut-paper pictures, each on its own scissor-cut card of a bright flat paper (lemon, apricot, mint, sky, pink), with a plain floor paper: large flat shapes, one down-right paper shadow, the LoC 1934 sheet's fibre as relative tone (cutpaper99.Cut); no ink line inside the pictures except object lettering

page 02's cut-paper agent (waistcoat, shirt sleeves, pencil) and clock (4:10), page 64's cut-paper stranger (cloche hat, coat, bag), cut larger here; a new cut-paper cupboard that opens on its left jamb, a brass key with its SERVICE tag on a hook, a blue SERVICE door with its card, desk, memo slip, think-puffs
under each card exactly one short sentence in the shared pen hand at cap 46; the four canon lines are quoted inside four of the sentences (no balloons, as in a picture book)
the memo slip in picture 1 is lettered as a note '4:15 - SERVICE / key - cupboard' (no full stops) so that the panel holds only its one sentence; the sentence under it states the memo
sentences: His memo says: open the SERVICE door at 4:15.
Off he goes to fetch the key from the cupboard.
A lady at the window asks, "Pardon me — have you the right time?"
He looks at the clock and says, "Ten past four, by the clock."
"Much obliged!" says the lady, and away she goes.
He opens the cupboard, and there hangs the brass key.
Pencil to his chin, he says, "Well, here I am... and what for?"
The key stays on its hook, and the SERVICE door stays shut.

events.E0: pictures 1-2: the memo on the desk; he walks toward the cupboard
events.E1: picture 3: the lady at the TICKET OFFICE window; the question in the sentence
events.E2: picture 4: the clock at 4:10; the answer in the sentence
events.E3: picture 5: she walks away from the window; the thanks in the sentence
events.E4: picture 6: the cupboard open, the brass key on its hook tagged SERVICE
events.E5: picture 7: pencil to his chin, the forgetting line in the sentence; picture 8: key on its hook, SERVICE door shut

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

substitutions: none: the four lines verbatim, quoted inside the panel sentences with a speaker tag; the memo text is given by the sentence under picture 1 and only as a note on the slip
beat: the book read aloud: the cards are laid one after another, each picture first, then its one sentence written beneath it
beat_frames: b07: + picture 7 and the forgetting sentence

self_check.check: Each panel has exactly one short sentence: each card carries one sentence beneath it (each ending in a single . ? or !, quoted lines counted inside their sentence); no balloon or caption inside the pictures; checked by the maker on the full page
self_check.evidence: perceptually judged (from the full page) by the maker; blind reading pending

weaknesses: sentences 3, 4 and 7 quote a canon line with its own dash or ellipsis inside, so each is one sentence with speech in it rather than the simplest picture-book sentence
the reused page-02 agent and page-64 stranger are more detailed (glasses, buttons) than the flat scenery; the stranger is small behind the counter in pictures 3 and 5
the memo slip in picture 1 carries a two-line note without full stops; a strict reader might count it as text in the panel
at phone width the ellipsis in 'here I am...' closes up to look like two dots
